summary:
# NOTES: "The Pillar of Light" by Louis Tracy (1904, Edward J. Clode, New York)

Epigraph: Matthew vii:25 ("...it fell not; for it was founded upon a rock"). Frontispieces: "LOW WATER--THE REEF", "THE GULF ROCK LIGHTHOUSE SECTION".

Chapters: I Flotsam; II A Christening; III The Signal; IV The Voice of the Reef; V The Hurricane; VI The Middle Watch; VII The Lottery; VIII An Interlude; IX Mrs. Vansittart; X Pyne's Progress; XI Mrs. Vansittart's Fear; XII Preparations; XIII Before the Dawn; XIV The Way They Have in The Navy; XV Enid's New Name; XVI Stephen Brand Explains; XVII Mrs. Vansittart Goes Home; XVIII Enid Wears an Old Ornament; XIX The House that Stood Upon a Rock.

## CH I (June morning, Gulf Rock Light, off Land's End/Scilly area)
- Gulf Rock lighthouse: granite column, ~130 ft above high water, reef beneath, great bell, occulting light, dioptric lens, 8-ring lantern, colza oil.
- Stephen Brand: assistant-keeper, gentleman, ~50 by later, ex-navy-trained, pipe-smoker, quotes Shelley ("Queen Mab"). Fled London two years earlier "with loathing akin to terror" (women/memory).
- Jim Spence (Jim): lame assistant (Egyptian campaign wound), Penzance/Marazion man, cheerful sailor, Cornish dialect ("cap'n", "ain't", "Dash them sea-crows").
- Jones: head keeper, recovering from sciatica, Baptist, "whitewash, polish, framed rules", wife, children, gossipy; keeps the "Pilchard and Seine" inn later.
- Thompson: third assistant, on shore leave.
- Steamer *Princess Royal* (NY to Southampton), ~8 miles off; its whistle blown four times in salute.
- Brand sees white-painted ship's lifeboat, broken mast, sail trailing, cormorants and gulls around it.
- Brand swims out (Jim warns of sharks; Brand: "This is not the Red Sea"); carries knife in sheath on belt.
- Blue shark (Carcharodon) attacks; Brand kills it with knife in two strokes (two gashes), boat-hook lashes its jaws to thole-pin.
- Brand dives/ fights; reaches boat; a dead man in boat, which Brand throws overboard.
- Under sail: live infant girl, wrapped in blanket, pinned with gold brooch (safety-pin type, four-leafed shamrock of small emeralds). Infant emaciated, ~1 year old, eyes raw.
- Jim feeds infant with milk-soaked handkerchief; Jones lowers basket with brandy and fresh milk.
- Brand: "It is a baby... I heard it cry."
- Jones finds vest marked "E. T." in white silk.
- Brand's theory: survivor died; child absorbed water through skin.
- Brand asks Jim and Jones to keep silence about shark.
- Brand says he will adopt child, write to Mrs. Sheppard (nurse of his own little girl, Constance). Brand is nephew of a baronet (rumor).
- Doctor came; child to Penzance; Mrs. Sheppard wrote note.
- Name chosen: **Trevillion** (surname, from Lyonnesse survivor); first name **Enid** (from Arthurian Enid, wife of Gawain); Jim's remark "Miss Enid Trevillion."
- Lyonnesse legend: sunken land between Land's End and Scilly.

## CH II (A Christening)
- Brand's silent, reticent about past; locked diary. Iliad translation for the keepers.
- Jim's remark: "a baby... baby is a girl by the duds."
- Brand's vacant reaction, "sat down rather suddenly."

## CH III (January, ~18 years later; Enid aged 19)
- Penzance harbor. Ben Pollard, old fisherman, boat *Daisy* (pilchard-driver). Cornish dialect ("'Ee knaw", "Miss Enid", "snaw", "norrard").
- Enid Trevillion: flaxen-haired, blue-eyed, green coat/skirt with dark red braid, white hat, white woolen jersey.
- Constance Brand: Brand's natural daughter, ~ hazel eyes, brown hair, Transatlantic poise; dressed like Enid.
- Lieutenant John Percival Stanhope, RN (Jack): mother Lady Margaret Stanhope (earl's daughter, Tregarthen Lodge, Penzance); father Sir Charles (deceased). Olive skin, blue eyes, Celtic. Recently ran HMS? ships into battleship mock-sink (initials stenciled on three battleships; ran into *Volcanic*).
- Morvah drive planned for next morning, 11 a.m.
- Storm rockets (three) signal "Help wanted"; snow squall; Ben turns back then continues; Brand signals "Bring a doctor" and rocket "Help wanted."
- Brand: Jackson (scalded hands) and Bates (broken leg, slipped on stairs) injured.
- Girls hoisted up in skip/basket.
- Ben: "Dang me... plucked 'uns."
- Stanhope commandeers steam-yacht *Lapwing* (10 tons; owner Mr. Lawton).
- Brand's 'Chief keeper Jones' contact.

## CH IV (Voice of the Reef)
- Bates and Jackson sent in *Daisy* to Penzance with Ben; Jackson helps lower Bates, says "Well done, Artie."
- Brand "Chapter"; "Chinook/Princess Royal"? (not here).
- Brand signals, *Lapwing* arrives with Stanhope in oilskins; semaphore: "Is all well?" "Bates and Jackson reached hospital," "L-o-v-e t-o E-n-i-d" "A-n-d C-o-n-s-t-a-n-c-e."
- Brand's auriscope (marine auriscope, directional sound detector) - girls learn it.
- Enid: "I suppose Jack will ask me to marry him."
- Brand: "I am fifty... world has aged."
- Brand's barometer falling; wind S.W. 6.

## CH V (The Hurricane)
- Enid: rescued 19 years ago, June 22nd. "Estimated" one year old.
- Brand's wife (Constance's mother) died when Constance 13 months old; buried at Brighton.
- Auriscope: picks up siren/fog horn; its pointer.
- *Lapwing* signalled "Landing impossible today."
- Brand's tea; Brand's relief due in a week; 21 years service.
- Barometer: 27.16°, thermometer 45.80° (1891 Northeast coast precedent).
- Hurricane at night; wind vane snapped. Brand tends lamp; "How can a man die better than at his post?"
- Enid cries: "Oh, dad, I am so frightened."

## CH VI (The Middle Watch)
- Brand sends girls to kitchen to make cocoa to get them away from lantern.
- Isaiah quotation "a refuge from the storm."
- Brand's "dochan doris" joke; laughs; Constance: "Audèo" (family motto).
- Brand smokes on duty; girls in pilot-coats. Brand gives heliograph mirror.
- Auriscope needle swings SW; a vessel approaching.
- Brand fires four rockets: three white, one red.
- A steamer (ship *Chinook*) disabled, drifting onto reef. Captain 'gallant'.
- Ship strikes reef; "There goes a fine ship, commanded by a brave man."

## CH VII (The Lottery)
- *Chinook* breaks in two; ~ survivors climbing; young Philadelphian **Charles A. Pyne** (nephew of Cyrus J. Traill) climbs fore-mast, throws rope line to gallery; truck of mast.
- Chief officer Emmett, junior officer first to reach gallery; Brand's arithmetic: 80 people.
- Captain goes down with ship, refusing to leave; Pyne's brief "Thank you, lad."
- Constance tends survivors (brandy); Pyne introduced ("Charles A. Pyne").
- Final count: 78 survivors.

## CH VIII (An Interlude)
- Hospital in visiting-officer's room; injured include stewardess and little girl.
- Enid and Pyne exchange: Pyne: "annex of heaven"; prospective step-aunt = **Mrs. Vansittart**, marrying Pyne's uncle Traill in Paris.
- Mrs. Vansittart (woman of 40): "Who are you? Tell me, child." Constance says "Constance Brand." Vansittart faints.
- Hymn singing on stairs; men threaten; Constance says they may smoke.
- Emmett and Brand: *Chinook* = former *Princess Royal*, renamed, captain Perkins (lost). Food: 81 people for 2 days 1/4. Brand's Rules and Regulations.
- Brand: "colza... vegetable oil."

## CH IX (Mrs. Vansittart)
- Survivors list: 37 officers/men, 33 saloon passengers (19 women), 7 men + 1 woman steerage.
- Mrs. Vansittart asks Enid about "Stephen Brand and his wife." Enid tells her story (E. T., boat).
- Mrs. Vansittart asks Constance to see Brand; Brand refuses to meet her (busy).
- Weeping.

## CH X (Pyne's Progress)
- Dawn; Brand signals *Chinook* news: "78 survivors... captain, 201 passengers, officers and crew lost."
- Stanhope on *Falcon*.
- Elsie and Mamie (Mrs. Taylor cares, mother drowned).
- Pyne gives his biscuit to kids; gives tea to kids.
- Brand: colza into food; Pyne says "Bi-sulphide of carbon..."
- Constance: "Mr. Pyne ... where is your cup?"

## CH XI (Mrs. Vansittart's Fear)
- Rationing; distilling via canvas coil; Pyne's jokes ("educated ass").
- Enid: "I am a mere waif."
- Mrs. Vansittart enters; Traill's telegram (wedding postponed/cancelled? She wants to leave for Penzance; train).
- Message: Traill on *Falcon*? "Mr. Cyrus J. Traill is on board."
- Mrs. Vansittart: "I quitted New York yesterday week in order to marry his uncle in Paris."

## CH XII (Preparations)
- Brand tells Pyne Enid received "proposal" by flag from Stanhope. Pyne: "Mother sends her love to Enid."
- Brand's plan: he alone (as keeper) would take food; fight; barricade. Pyne refuses to leave Mrs. Vansittart.
- Pyne steals? Brand takes tins from store-room; Pyne's rescue of two kids; raft attempt.
- Raft from Trinity tender fails; "Will try again next tide."

## CH XIII (Before the Dawn)
- Emmett ill; German from Chicago: "Vere's de goot..."
- Methylated spirits drunk by mutineers; Brand's rain; rain collected small amount.
- Pyne/Brand talk: Pyne's family: father's yacht *Esmeralda* lost; uncle lost wife & child; Pyne 6 years old at time.
- Mrs. Vansittart appears at door; asks if Brand knows her; "Mistaken."
- Mrs. Vansittart weeping outside bedroom: "I dare not..."

## CH XIV (The Way They Have in The Navy)
- Enid burns finger; Pyne doubts storeroom missing items.
- Brand/Stanhope: Stanhope rows boat to rock with Ben Pollard and Jim Spence.
- Brand pours colza oil on sea to calm waves ("Follow me!"). Oil scattered by hand.
- Stanhope throws rope; Brand's line; Stanhope tied to boat.
- Enid recognizes Ben and Jim.

## CH XV (Enid's New Name)
- Rope secured; messages; food sent in water-tight tins.
- Traill: "Did you see her?" Traill pays Ben & Jim £500 each.
- Pyne's letter: Traill's letter: Enid is Traill's daughter **Edith Traill**; "E. T." mark; brooch; Mr. Jones (retired keeper) informed Traill.
- Brand: "Why should I hate anyone who brings rank..." Pyne: "Oh, bully!"

## CH XVI (Stephen Brand Explains)
- Elsie & Mamie see "the milkman."
- Stanhope boards rock; kisses Enid.
- Mrs. Vansittart leaves rock; Traill asks her; "Don't kiss me."
- Hotel dinner; Brand arrives; Mrs. Vansittart faints; Brand: "When I knew her her name was Nanette... my wife."
- Constance: "Do you mean that she is my mother?"

## CH XVII (Mrs. Vansittart Goes Home)
- Brand's full story: Sir Stephen Brand, ninth baronet, of Lesser Hambledon, Northumberland; was attaché at British Embassy, Paris; married Madeleine Nanette de Courtray (Jersey); duel with French fop, killed him; wife went to him; divorce in Nebraska on desertion ground.
- Mrs. Sheppard brought infant Constance to England.
- Lady Margaret: son Stanhope says Enid is Traill's daughter; Traill's settlement £200,000.
- Mrs. Vansittart arrives at cottage; collapses at gate; Constance: "Dad, she has come home."
- Police sergeant Jenkins.

## CH XVIII (Enid Wears an Old Ornament)
- Lady Margaret departs; Stanhope.
- Traill narrates *Esmeralda* disaster: July 21 fog between Scilly and Fastnet; struck by barque *John S.* (Nova Scotian); Pyne (nephew) 6 years; Edith Traill 6 months old; Brand found boat 30 July.
- Brooch bought in Bergen.
- Mrs. Vansittart's letters: Pyne (to care for kids); Traill (cannot marry).
- Mrs. Vansittart departed to London. Actually Sergeant Jenkins reports she is at Brand's house.
- Enid wears brooch; Traill: "you are very like your mother."

## CH XIX (The House that Stood Upon a Rock)
- Week later; Enid at Emmett, Jones, Jim Spence.
- Brand meets Nanette in cottage; she begs forgiveness; she obtained divorce in Nebraska on desertion; she married Traill engagement.
- Brand forgives; she asks to stay.
- Weddings: Pyne & Constance (Mr. and Mrs. Pyne to Italy); Stanhope & Enid (Lieut. and Mrs. Stanhope to Riviera); Brand & Nanette (remarried in Nebraska; wedding in May, north-country mansion).
- Final: steamer past Gulf Rock; "winking portentously... running away with your own wife."

THE END.
